result.defense: C wins because it meets the binding acceptance path A explicitly misses and B meets only at disproportionate risk. Against A: A admits criterion 2 is NOT met, leaves 28 sidebar stops, and makes row actions reachable only via the undiscoverable ContextMenu/Shift+F10 route; C adds a ~60-line useRovingTabindex hook, data-roving on existing rows/links/headers, tabIndex=-1 actions opened by ArrowRight/ContextMenu/Shift+F10, and :focus-within visibility, so the sidebar becomes one stop per group in 2-3 days. Against B: B meets all criteria on paper, but requires extracting an 8000+ line Shell.tsx shared with VIS-01/02/04, new tree/feed ARIA, F6 (browser-conflicting), j/k shortcuts, and app-wide form work overlapping VIS-06 - 1-2 weeks with streaming, drag-reorder, and screen-reader regression risk. C reuses A's proven core (skip link to [data-skip-target] composer/main, single full-strength --ring 2px outline at 4-5:1, dialog finalFocus, Auth error summary) plus established GitHub/Linear conventions, achieving criteria 1-4 and 6 and the Auth case of 5 without markup rewrites or new interaction vocabulary.

result.defense: Proposal C is the only option that satisfies every acceptance criterion without risking a multi-week rewrite of `Shell.tsx`. It fixes the 2:1 focus ring contrast across all controls using the existing `--ring` token at full opacity plus a global `:focus-visible` fallback, lands the skip link directly in the chat composer (`[data-skip-target]`) or `main`, restores dialog focus via `finalFocus` (with a named fallback if the opener unmounts, as in `CapTable.tsx`), and collapses the 41 sidebar stops into roving tabindex groups via a lightweight 60-line `[data-roving]` hook where row actions reveal on `:focus-within` and open with `ArrowRight` (crucial for Mac keyboards that lack a ContextMenu key). Proposal A fails Criteria 1 and 2 outright by leaving 28 tab stops in the sidebar with no arrow-key roving and hiding row actions behind `Shift+F10`/ContextMenu without visual affordance. Proposal B meets the criteria but over-engineers the shell: extracting a new `SidebarNav` (`role="tree"`), `Feed` (`role="feed"`), and `FocusRegions` (`F6`, which conflicts with native browser pane cycling) out of an 8,000-line `Shell.tsx` creates severe merge conflicts with VIS-01/02/04, overlaps VIS-06 on global form errors, and risks breaking drag-and-drop reordering and streaming scroll anchoring.
